relationship_to_primary_plan: supplementary robustness check on the already-written judged-divergence plan; the primary endpoint stays the hand-blind depth-4 judge. This variant was conceived after the primary aggregate was seen, so it is explicitly exploratory and cannot change the primary verdict.
question: Are the depth-4 verdicts of the primary judged-divergence run stable when the depth-4 judge itself carries hand_weight 0.9 instead of 0.0? A judge that shares the blind arm's evaluator could favour blind-style moves by construction, which would make 'the deeper search prefers the blind move' partly a judge-configuration artefact.
method: identical reconstruction, identical first-divergence positions, identical candidate moves (asserted against the saved move lists exactly as in the primary run); only the depth-4 judge's EvaluationConfig.hand_weight changes 0.0 -> 0.9; no depth-6 tie-break (--no-tie-break) so this variant adds no new endpoint.
inputs: the same four served-blind result files under .local_agent/hand-utility-games-20261018/

guards.no_overwrite: refuses to write an existing result path

reported_quantities: per-cell sign agreement between the two judges, the paired 2x2 verdict table, and the subset of cells whose absolute delta is mate-scale (>= 1e6)

fixed_weight_curve.purpose: a third fixed judge point at double the served coefficient, used only to test whether the shared verdict drift is monotone in the judge's own hand_weight; it adds no new endpoint, no selection over weights and no search beyond the declared 400/900 guards
fixed_weight_curve.prediction_if_judge_coefficient_explains: served_better count increases from 0.0 to 0.9 to 1.8 while the mate-scale cells keep their sign

done_condition: second result file written, agreement table produced by the reader, README/claim note added
limitations_prewritten: two fixed judges, neither is ground truth
same 45 pair-cells / 35 distinct positions; depth-2 and depth-3 cells can share one judged position, so the two judges' agreement is not independent replication
no significance claim, no strength/generality claim, no product change
